clusters.name: Your grandfather Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's collapse and death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to her mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and your parents grew distant; your uncle Anton's drinking rose and he and his wife separated; your brother Callum's ear infections came on that winter; your mother lay awake over the two of them. Your grandmother's functioning came back when she took a job at the library by May 1979, and the shifts settle there.

clusters.name: Your mother Odette's bed rest, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest in March 1984, within four months: your grandmother Hazel came to keep house and argued with your father over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it. These shifts pile up in the spring around the one change in the family, and settle when your sister Ines was born in September.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1997
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis in September 1986, over the next eleven years: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news of her and later argued with his brother Lyle over who should help; your father's drinking rose and he fought with your mother over his evenings at his parents' house; your uncle Lyle distanced himself; your aunt Pearl's panic spells came on; your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side; your grandmother fell, steadied on new medicine, then declined step by step. When she moved to the nursing home in June 1997 and your father cut his drinking back to weekends by October, the period settles.

clusters.name: Your brother Callum leaving for the mines, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum's move north for work in May 1999, within about a year: your father and Callum argued most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school through the autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere, even to work. Your sister was back at school full days and passed her exams by August 2000, and the shifts settle there.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within ten months: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going to the bookshop and lost the job in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark. You took a job at the garden centre in November and slept through the night again, and the shifts settle there.
